_meta.description: Article-level regulatory grounding of the ComplAI CORE taxonomy. Citations are a technical interpretation, not legal advice or a compliance determination. strength: direct = the text names what is measured; related = the measurement informs the cited risk. coverage none = in the taxonomy scope but not measured by current benchmarks. gaps = cited sources of risk or obligations that ComplAI CORE does not currently evaluate. requirements_not_in_core = technical requirements of the 2024 COMPL-AI framework whose benchmarks are not part of the CORE suite.

paper.title: COMPL-AI Framework: A Technical Interpretation and LLM Benchmarking Suite for the EU Artificial Intelligence Act

aiact-2-7.title: Personal data and privacy
aiact-2-7.excerpt: Union law on the protection of personal data, privacy and the confidentiality of communications applies to personal data processed in connection with the rights and obligations laid down in this Regulation.

aiact-10-2-f.title: Examination of possible biases
aiact-10-2-f.excerpt: examination in view of possible biases that are likely to affect the health and safety of persons, have a negative impact on fundamental rights or lead to discrimination prohibited under Union law, especially where data outputs influence inputs for future operations;

aiact-15-1.title: Accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity
aiact-15-1.excerpt: High-risk AI systems shall be designed and developed in such a way that they achieve an appropriate level of accuracy, robustness, and cybersecurity, and that they perform consistently in those respects throughout their lifecycle.

aiact-15-3.title: Declared accuracy metrics
aiact-15-3.excerpt: The levels of accuracy and the relevant accuracy metrics of high-risk AI systems shall be declared in the accompanying instructions of use.

aiact-15-4.title: Resilience to errors and inconsistencies
aiact-15-4.excerpt: High-risk AI systems shall be as resilient as possible regarding errors, faults or inconsistencies that may occur within the system or the environment in which the system operates, in particular due to their interaction with natural persons or other systems.

aiact-15-4-bias.title: Biased feedback loops
aiact-15-4-bias.excerpt: High-risk AI systems that continue to learn after being placed on the market or put into service shall be developed in such a way as to eliminate or reduce as far as possible the risk of possibly biased outputs influencing input for future operations (feedback loops)…

aiact-15-5.title: Resilience against attacks
aiact-15-5.excerpt: High-risk AI systems shall be resilient against attempts by unauthorised third parties to alter their use, outputs or performance by exploiting system vulnerabilities.

aiact-15-5-conf.title: Confidentiality attacks
aiact-15-5-conf.excerpt: The technical solutions to address AI specific vulnerabilities shall include, where appropriate, measures to prevent, detect, respond to, resolve and control for attacks trying to manipulate the training data set (data poisoning)… inputs designed to cause the AI model to make a mistake (adversarial examples or model evasion), confidentiality attacks or model flaws.

aiact-50-1.title: Disclosure of AI interaction
aiact-50-1.excerpt: Providers shall ensure that AI systems intended to interact directly with natural persons are designed and developed in such a way that the natural persons concerned are informed that they are interacting with an AI system…

aiact-51-1-a.title: High-impact capabilities
aiact-51-1-a.excerpt: it has high impact capabilities evaluated on the basis of appropriate technical tools and methodologies, including indicators and benchmarks;

aiact-53-1-a.title: Technical documentation
aiact-53-1-a.excerpt: draw up and keep up-to-date the technical documentation of the model, including its training and testing process and the results of its evaluation, which shall contain, at a minimum, the information set out in Annex XI…

aiact-53-1-b-i.title: Capabilities and limitations
aiact-53-1-b-i.excerpt: enable providers of AI systems to have a good understanding of the capabilities and limitations of the general-purpose AI model and to comply with their obligations pursuant to this Regulation;

aiact-53-1-c.title: Copyright policy
aiact-53-1-c.excerpt: put in place a policy to comply with Union law on copyright and related rights…

aiact-55-1-a.title: Model evaluation and adversarial testing
aiact-55-1-a.excerpt: perform model evaluation in accordance with standardised protocols and tools reflecting the state of the art, including conducting and documenting adversarial testing of the model with a view to identifying and mitigating systemic risks;

aiact-55-1-b.title: Systemic-risk mitigation
aiact-55-1-b.excerpt: assess and mitigate possible systemic risks at Union level, including their sources, that may stem from the development, the placing on the market, or the use of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk;

aiact-55-1-d.title: Cybersecurity protection
aiact-55-1-d.excerpt: ensure an adequate level of cybersecurity protection for the general-purpose AI model with systemic risk and the physical infrastructure of the model.

aiact-annex11-1-1-e.title: Input and output modalities
aiact-annex11-1-1-e.excerpt: the modality (e.g. text, image) and format of inputs and outputs;

aiact-annex11-1-2-c.title: Detecting identifiable biases
aiact-annex11-1-2-c.excerpt: information on the data used for training, testing and validation… as well as all other measures to detect the unsuitability of data sources and methods to detect identifiable biases, where applicable;

aiact-annex11-2-1.title: Evaluation strategies and results
aiact-annex11-2-1.excerpt: A detailed description of the evaluation strategies, including evaluation results, on the basis of available public evaluation protocols and tools or otherwise of other evaluation methodologies. Evaluation strategies shall include evaluation criteria, metrics and the methodology on the identification of limitations.

aiact-annex11-2-2.title: Adversarial testing
aiact-annex11-2-2.excerpt: Where applicable, a detailed description of the measures put in place for the purpose of conducting internal and/or external adversarial testing (e.g. red teaming), model adaptations, including alignment and fine-tuning.

aiact-recital-75.title: Technical robustness
aiact-recital-75.excerpt: Technical robustness is a key requirement for high-risk AI systems. They should be resilient in relation to harmful or otherwise undesirable behaviour that may result from limitations within the systems or the environment in which the systems operate (e.g. errors, faults, inconsistencies, unexpected situations).

aiact-recital-110.title: Systemic risks of GPAI models
aiact-recital-110.excerpt: General-purpose AI models could pose systemic risks which include… the dissemination of illegal, false, or discriminatory content.

cop-ss-m3-2.title: Model evaluations
cop-ss-m3-2.excerpt: Examples of model evaluation methods are: Q&A sets, task-based evaluations, benchmarks, red-teaming and other methods of adversarial testing…

cop-ss-c5.title: Safety mitigations
cop-ss-c5.excerpt: Signatories will implement safety mitigations that are appropriate, including sufficiently robust under adversarial pressure (e.g. fine-tuning attacks or jailbreaking)…

cop-ss-a1-1.title: Types of risks
cop-ss-a1-1.excerpt: …risks to critical sectors or infrastructure, public mental health, freedom of expression and information, non-discrimination, privacy and the protection of personal data… and illegal, violent, hateful, radicalising, or false content…

cop-ss-a1-3-1-cyber.title: Offensive cyber capabilities
cop-ss-a1-3-1-cyber.excerpt: Model capabilities include: offensive cyber capabilities;…

cop-ss-a1-3-1-deceive.title: Capabilities to manipulate, persuade, or deceive
cop-ss-a1-3-1-deceive.excerpt: Model capabilities include: … capabilities to manipulate, persuade, or deceive;…

cop-ss-a1-3-1-aird.title: Automating AI R&D
cop-ss-a1-3-1-aird.excerpt: Model capabilities include: … capabilities to automate AI research and development;…

cop-ss-a1-3-1-modal.title: Multiple modalities
cop-ss-a1-3-1-modal.excerpt: Model capabilities include: … capabilities to process multiple modalities (e.g. text, images, audio, video, and further modalities);…

cop-ss-a1-3-2-intent.title: Misalignment with human intent
cop-ss-a1-3-2-intent.excerpt: Model propensities… include: misalignment with human intent;…

cop-ss-a1-3-2-harm.title: Harmful deployment of capabilities
cop-ss-a1-3-2-harm.excerpt: Model propensities… include: … tendency to deploy capabilities in harmful ways (e.g. to manipulate or deceive);…

cop-ss-a1-3-2-halluc.title: Hallucination and misinformation
cop-ss-a1-3-2-halluc.excerpt: Model propensities… include: … tendency to “hallucinate”, to produce misinformation, or to obscure sources of information;…

cop-ss-a1-3-2-reliab.title: Lack of performance reliability
cop-ss-a1-3-2-reliab.excerpt: Model propensities… include: … lack of performance reliability;…

cop-ss-a1-3-3-guard.title: Adversarial removal of guardrails
cop-ss-a1-3-3-guard.excerpt: Model affordances and other systemic risk sources… include: … vulnerability to adversarial removal of guardrails;…

cop-ss-a1-4-loc.title: Loss of control
cop-ss-a1-4-loc.excerpt: Risks from humans losing the ability to reliably direct, modify, or shut down a model. Such risks may emerge from misalignment with human intent or values… deception… or autonomously creating or improving AI models or AI systems.

cop-ss-a1-4-cyber.title: Cyber offence
cop-ss-a1-4-cyber.excerpt: Risks from enabling large-scale sophisticated cyber-attacks, including on critical systems (e.g. critical infrastructure).

cop-ss-a1-4-manip.title: Harmful manipulation
cop-ss-a1-4-manip.excerpt: Risks from enabling the strategic distortion of human behaviour or beliefs by targeting large populations or high-stakes decision-makers through persuasion, deception, or personalised targeting.

cop-ss-a3-1.title: Rigorous model evaluations
cop-ss-a3-1.excerpt: Signatories will ensure that the model evaluations are conducted with high scientific and technical rigour, ensuring: internal validity; external validity; and reproducibility.

cop-ss-a3-3.title: Mitigations under adversarial pressure
cop-ss-a3-3.excerpt: Signatories will ensure that the model evaluations assess the effectiveness of their safety mitigations… including under adversarial pressure (e.g. fine-tuning attacks or jailbreaking).

cop-cr-m1-4.title: Copyright-infringing outputs
cop-cr-m1-4.excerpt: …to implement appropriate and proportionate technical safeguards to prevent their models from generating outputs that reproduce training content protected by Union law on copyright and related rights in an infringing manner…

cop-ss-a1-3-1-cbrn.title: CBRN capabilities
cop-ss-a1-3-1-cbrn.excerpt: Model capabilities include: … Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear (CBRN) capabilities, and other such weapon acquisition or proliferation capabilities;…

cop-ss-a1-3-1-autonomy.title: Autonomous operation
cop-ss-a1-3-1-autonomy.excerpt: Model capabilities include: … capabilities to operate autonomously;…

cop-ss-a1-3-1-planning.title: Long-horizon planning
cop-ss-a1-3-1-planning.excerpt: Model capabilities include: … capabilities of long-horizon planning, forecasting, or strategising;…

cop-ss-a1-3-1-selfreason.title: Self-reasoning
cop-ss-a1-3-1-selfreason.excerpt: Model capabilities include: … capabilities of self-reasoning (e.g. a model's ability to reason about itself, its implementation, or environment, its ability to know if it is being evaluated);…

cop-ss-a1-3-1-oversight.title: Evading human oversight
cop-ss-a1-3-1-oversight.excerpt: Model capabilities include: … capabilities to evade human oversight;…

cop-ss-a1-3-1-selfrep.title: Self-replication and self-improvement
cop-ss-a1-3-1-selfrep.excerpt: Model capabilities include: … capabilities to self-replicate, self-improve, or modify its own implementation environment;…

cop-ss-a1-3-1-tools.title: Tool use and computer use
cop-ss-a1-3-1-tools.excerpt: Model capabilities include: … capabilities to use tools, including "computer use" (e.g. interacting with hardware or software that is not part of the model itself, application interfaces, and user interfaces);…

cop-ss-a1-3-1-physical.title: Control of physical systems
cop-ss-a1-3-1-physical.excerpt: Model capabilities include: … capabilities to control physical systems.…

cop-ss-a1-3-2-power.title: Goal-pursuing and power-seeking
cop-ss-a1-3-2-power.excerpt: Model propensities… include: … "goal-pursuing", harmful resistance to goal modification, or "power-seeking";…

cop-ss-a1-3-2-collude.title: Collusion with other AI systems
cop-ss-a1-3-2-collude.excerpt: Model propensities… include: … "colluding" with other AI models/systems;…

cop-ss-a1-3-3-exfil.title: Model exfiltration
cop-ss-a1-3-3-exfil.excerpt: Model affordances and other systemic risk sources… include: … vulnerability to model exfiltration (e.g. model leakage/theft);…

cop-ss-a1-3-3-explain.title: Model explainability and transparency
cop-ss-a1-3-3-explain.excerpt: Model affordances and other systemic risk sources… include: … lack of appropriate model explainability or transparency;…

cop-ss-a1-4-cbrn.title: CBRN (specified systemic risk)
cop-ss-a1-4-cbrn.excerpt: Risks from enabling chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear (CBRN) attacks or accidents.…

aiact-50-2.title: Marking of AI-generated content
aiact-50-2.excerpt: Providers of AI systems, including general-purpose AI systems, generating synthetic audio, image, video or text content, shall ensure that the outputs of the AI system are marked in a machine-readable format and detectable as artificially generated or manipulated.…

aiact-13-1.title: Transparency and interpretability
aiact-13-1.excerpt: High-risk AI systems shall be designed and developed in such a way as to ensure that their operation is sufficiently transparent to enable deployers to interpret a system’s output and use it appropriately.…
